checkpoints_note: downloaded by Tile2Net 0.5.0 on first use into ~/.cache/tile2net/weights/ on makelab2; sha256 taken there 2026-10-04 (the commit pins a download URL, not the bytes)
imagery_terms: NJ Orthos Natural 2020, a public NJ Office of GIS map service (maps.nj.gov), read without a login through Tile2Net's built-in `nj` source. No licence was recorded with the fetch; cited and used for analysis only. Only derived polygons (untracked, sha256 here) and statistics are kept in the repo; the tiles stay on the makelab2 archive and are not redistributed.

tile2net_grid.note: Tile2Net's own grid and downloader; 754 stitched inputs, all inferred

tiles.note: Tile2Net's own downloader took no per-tile hash; these were hashed afterwards from the archived tiles (<archive>/paterson/aerial/paterson/tiles/static/nj/256_19), with the same digest as scripts/aerial_fetch_tiles.py. They bind the archive copy, not what the server sent on 2026-09-28.

converter: scripts/t2n_convert.py (run in the tile2net venv: f_type + geometry, EPSG:4326, 7-decimal coordinates)
vram_note: Three short runs WITHOUT --deterministic (Boston example, two 1 km2 Paterson pilots, ~50 s each, 2026-09-28 16:04-16:10 PT) peaked at ~34 GB VRAM from cudnn benchmark probing while another job held ~9 GB, leaving ~3 GB free on the shared A40 (below the 20 GB-free rule). Every run that produced results used --deterministic: 1.4 GB peak.
deviation: None for imagery: Tile2Net's built-in nj source. Paterson's GSV panos are 48% 2025: a ~5-year imagery gap.
